description:
16 years old Egyptian baccalaureate student in medicine and life science track. 

Interested in astronomy. I want to connect my love of space with medicine and do a simple project to demonstrate how the health of astronauts is monitored.
summary: EyeMars is a lightweight health monitoring software designed for long-duration space missions. It helps astronauts track vital health indicators like heart rate, eye health, stress, and sleep in real-time. The system uses NASA open data and simple AI analysis to detect early changes caused by space radiation, isolation, and microgravity. It provides alerts, personalized advice, and a simple dashboard so astronauts can evaluate and act on their health independently when communication with Earth is limited. Our goal is to make space healthcare accessible, preventive, and human-centered.
details:
EyeMars is a health monitoring software for astronauts on long-duration missions to Moon and Mars.
What it does: It tracks daily vitals - heart rate, eye health, sleep, and mood - and detects early risks from space radiation, microgravity, and isolation.
How it works: 1) Astronaut does quick daily check-in. 2) Software analyzes trends using simple AI to detect SANS (eye swelling), stress, and fatigue. 3) Dashboard shows green/yellow/red status with personalized advice like rest, water, or exercise. Data is stored locally for use when Earth contact is delayed.
Benefits: Keeps astronauts healthy without needing a doctor on board, very important when far from Earth.
Intended impact: Make space healthcare preventive, simple, and human-centered.
Tools: Figma for UI prototype, Python for data logic, Google Docs for documentation.
Creativity: Combines medical astronomy with simple visuals that an astronaut can understand in seconds under stress, not complex medical charts
